item.title: Toxic Aerosol Evacuates Arena, Tankers Burn, Climate Talks Collapse: On Air, November 24, 2026
item.description:
American rapper Don Toliver postponed a London concert after an unknown substance was released inside the Co-op Live arena in Manchester during a performance, prompting the evacuation of more than 12,000 fans. Greater Manchester Police declared a major incident at approximately 10 p.m. on Sunday as emergency services arrived at the venue following reports of audience members experiencing coughing, breathing difficulties, and a powerful smell. First responders assessed 88 people at the scene for respiratory and eye symptoms, and one person was transported to the hospital.
President Donald Trump delivered remarks at the Justice Department headquarters in Washington to denounce California Governor Gavin Newsom and his plan to commute the sentences of more than 500 California death row inmates to life in prison. Trump was joined by Attorney General Todd Blanche, FBI Director Kash Patel, and several relatives of murder victims who spoke in opposition to the commutation plan. Trump announced a presidential directive ordering the Justice Department to seek the death penalty in federal child murder cases and certain capital crimes involving rape and kidnapping.
Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, coinciding with Victory Day, her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali announced. It is the first time Hasina has publicly set a specific date for her return after fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising. Hasina urged Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her air transport from Delhi aboard Biman Bangladesh Airlines, arguing that the government bears responsibility for her security.
Malaysia will send more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar in a new round of repatriations, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced. The announcement comes five days after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar's security forces committed genocide against the Rohingya minority. Anwar told parliament that 1,500 Myanmar nationals will be returned on three naval vessels on December 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will be returned by aircraft during December at the expense of the Malaysian government. Turkey rejected Malaysia's request to accept Rohingya refugees due to its existing refugee population.
The United Nations climate summit ended in collapse on Sunday in Antalya, Turkey, after nearly two weeks of negotiations broke down over fossil fuel references and financial commitments. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who serves as Australia's climate minister, conceded he could not overcome unbridgeable red lines as the summit ran more than two days beyond schedule into forty-four hours of overtime. A proposed agreement failed after countries including European Union members, Panama, and developing nation blocs rejected compromise texts on emissions phase-outs and climate finance contributions. Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum blamed the European Union for taking an imposing stance during the final hours.
Israeli airstrikes killed at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, local health and police officials reported. Medics stated that three people, including two police officers, were killed in an airstrike at a police post in Khan Younis in southern Gaza, while five others were wounded. A separate Israeli airstrike near the Netzarim corridor further north killed another three people. The Israeli military stated that it struck fighters in both areas without providing further details.
A federal appeals court denied an emergency motion to halt the planned detonation of nearly five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Iran Vows to Confront United States Naval Blockade With Available Tools: On Air, November 23, 2026
item.description:
Iran announced on Monday that it would use all available means to counter a United States naval blockade imposed during the ongoing conflict. Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei stated during a press briefing in Tehran that the economic sanctions and naval blockade constitute military aggression, and that Iran is entitled to use any means for self-defense under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter.
President Donald Trump hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, on Sunday night. The event brought together a couple dozen men in suits and featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, Shark Tank investor Kevin O'Leary, and former NBA star Tristan Thompson.
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed stated that he is open to working with President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance to enact universal healthcare under the name TrumpCare, arguing that the title does not matter if it guarantees coverage for all Americans. The proposal follows remarks by President Trump during a Friday press conference indicating openness to a combination of healthcare ideas.
Russian forces launched a massive aerial assault involving 153 attack and decoy drones against railway, energy, and civilian infrastructure across 12 oblasts and Kyiv, killing at least six people and injuring 32 others. Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi reported strikes on railway station grounds in Dnipro and Zhytomyr Oblast, a locomotive depot and electrical substations in Kharkiv, and a hotel in Kharkiv.
Israeli political leaders and officials condemned a wave of arson attacks and vandalism carried out by Jewish extremists in Palestinian villages across the occupied West Bank, primarily in the Ramallah area and the South Hebron Hills, where vehicles were torched and racist graffiti was sprayed.
Washington state and local leaders sharply rebuked Immigration and Customs Enforcement after masked federal officers detained two passengers on a crowded jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The incident occurred on Saturday morning as passengers were boarding an Alaska Airlines flight bound for Los Angeles, causing a distressing scene that delayed the flight.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: Trilateral Peace Pact Signed While Baltic Ship Burns: On Air, November 22, 2026
item.description:
A Russian cargo ship remains on fire and anchored in Finnish waters after sustaining a drone strike in the Baltic Sea in international waters west of Gogland island. The sixteen crew members of the 121-meter vessel named the Sparta II abandoned ship for lifeboats before transferring safely to a nearby Russian merchant vessel while rescue ships deployed water cannons. Finnish military and political leadership stated that Ukraine was likely responsible for the strike.
Mexican security forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, also known as Chapo Isidro, during a special forces raid in the town of Guasave in Sinaloa state. The operation triggered intense clashes that left four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen dead while cartel members mounted resistance and set up roadblocks.
United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin convened in Shenzhen, China, for the first dedicated trilateral meeting between the sitting heads of state of the three nations. The leaders issued a four-point joint peace declaration committing to reduce nuclear risks, reconfigure international institutions, and free up global energy supply lines. Trump defended his relationships with Putin and Xi during subsequent remarks at the White House.
A fire swept through the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in the Serang district of Banten province in Indonesia, leaving at least three workers dead and approximately fifty individuals unaccounted for. Emergency rescue teams recovered body bags from the three-story building, which produces Milkita brand snacks, while firefighters battled flames and carried out cooling operations over a day after the blaze broke out. Fifteen workers were rescued alive from the site, with several hospitalized for injuries.
President Donald Trump confirmed in a Fox News interview that the Federal Bureau of Investigation National Crime Information Center database was targeted in a cyberattack. The computer system stores criminal justice records, including fingerprints, wanted persons profiles, violent felons data, missing persons reports, and historical files used by federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies. The breach constitutes the second recent cybersecurity incident affecting the bureau following a September attack on its job portal.
Bahrain reported that an Iranian strike targeted a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, sparking a fire and injuring two people on Sitra Island near a Bapco refinery. The Interior Ministry stated that a Pakistani resident was in critical condition and a Bahraini citizen was in stable condition following the attack. Iran Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for the strike, stating that aerospace forces launched operations against military installations.
Masked immigration officers detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding an aircraft, delaying a flight bound for Los Angeles. The airline described the incident as distressing for travelers and employees on site.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham secured a reset package at a Brussels summit alongside European Union officials, covering food checks, emissions trading, and youth mobility. The youth mobility program will allow up to 100,000 young Europeans to enter Britain annually to travel, work, volunteer, and study for up to three years.
A Russian drone strike partially destroyed a five-storey residential building in the village of Dymer in Kyiv Oblast on Sunday morning, leaving one person dead and three injured while emergency workers searched for 14 missing people. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that rescue teams evacuated nine residents and contained the fire at the site.
